description.narrative:
Ipas is a nonprofit organisatíon based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, US. They work in 16 countries and have three regional offices. Ipas requests SEK 312.500.000 in core support for the period Fiscal Years (FY) 2018 - 2023, to continue the partnership with Sida with the ultimate goal of eliminating unsafe abortion and ensure access to contraceptives. Sida's contribution is 8% of the total budget of USD 428 436 000. Sida and six other donors are providing core support with a number of smaller donors providing restricted funding. Ipas will meet the reproductive health needs of women and girls by creating enabling environments that support the access to high-quality abortion and contraceptive care; ensure that high-quality abortion and contraceptive care are available, accessible, and acceptable; and ensure that women and girls have the social support, knowledge, and self-efficacy to access safe abortion and contraception. The core support is to enable Ipas to implement its strategic plan (SP) FY 2018 - 2023.
lpas is working to strengthen health systems, policy & advocacy (at global, regional and national leves), training providers on abortion care, community engagement & stigma reduction, research, integration of abortion and contraception in humanitarian and sexual education through support to civil society actors, as well as provision of abortion services, equipment and counseling in public health services in 16 countries, three regional programs as well as globally. The programme focus on Africa where the needs are considered the highest.
By the end of Ipas' strategic plan,will result in 3.8 million unsafe abortions averted (7% of the total of unsafe abortions in the countries where Ipas works); 6% of all abortions in countries (4.9M) will be performed at Ipas- supported facilities and 4% of unitended pregnancies (7.7 M) will be averted.

Ipas är en icke vinstdrivande organisation med huvudkontor i Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA och som verkar i 16 länder och har tre regionala kontor. Ipas har ansökt om 312.500.000 kr i kärnstöd för deras strategiska plan (SP), Fiscal Years 2018-2023. Den totala budgeten för SP är 428 436 000 USD. Sida:s bidrag utgör 8% av den totala budgeten. Det är en ökning på 17 % årligen sedan tidigare kärnstöd för Ipas SP 2014 - 2017, men procentsatsen för Sidas totala bidrag ligger kvar på 8%. Ipas har sex andra kärnstödsgivare och ett antal mindre givare som ger öronmärkta bidrag. Syftet med Ipas SP är att eliminera osäker abort och säkerställa tillgång till preventivmedel. Ipas arbetar för att möta kvinnors och flickors reproduktiva hälsobehov genom att skapa möjligheter som stöder tillgången och tillgängligheten till acceptabla abort och preventivmedel av hög kvalitet samt försäkra att kvinnor och flickor har socialt stöd, kunskap och förmåga att söka och få tillgång till abort och preventivmedel, om de så önskar.
lpas arbetar med att stärka hälsosystem, påverkansarbete, kunskapsspridning, kapacitetshöjande utbildning av hälsopersonal, forskning, integrering av abort och preventivmedel inom humanitärt arbete och inom sexualundervisningen genom vidareförmedling av mindre bidrag till civilsamhällsaktörer samt med tillhandahållande av aborttjänster, utrustning och rådgivning inom den offentliga hälso- och sjukvården i 16 länder, tre regionala program och globalt. Programverksamheten fokuserar på Afrika där behoven anses störst.
Ipas förväntar att deras arbete ska resultera i att 3,8 miljoner osäkra aborter avvärjs (7% av antalet osäkra aborter i de länder där Ipas arbetar), 6% av alla aborter i deras programländer (4,9M) kommer att utföras hos Ipas-stödda anläggningar och 4% av oplanerade graviditeter (7,7 M) kommer att avvärjas.

VISSION: A world where every woman and girl has the right and ability to determine her own sexuality and reproductive health MISSION: Women and girls have improved sexual and reproductive health and rights through enhanced access to and use of safe abortion and contraceptive care. ULTIMATE OUTCOME: Sustainable abortion eco-system INTEMEDIATE OUTCOME 1: Improved policies, laws and financing INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 2: Enhanced agency and social norms INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 2: Improved access, availability, quality and acceptability
Crosscutting outcome: Reduced abortion stigma
All Ipas interventions are to be guided by the following principles: Human rights and equity, Woman-centered, local expertise, partnership and collaboration, ownership and accountability.

Ipas has contributed to strong results during FY23. Some of the highlights include:
- 456,917 abortion services were provided at Ipas-supported access points across 25 countries, out of which 429,224 wre provided at Ipas-supported health facilities and 27,063 were self-managed abortion (SMA) services supported through SMA access points across 16 countries. This is a 32% increase from FY22 and is driven by SMA programming scale-up in Mexico, DRC, Nigeria, Bolivia, and Kenya, and launch in Ethiopia.
- Ipas-supported access points provided 335,640 postabortion contraceptive services. 85% of postabortion clients (both facility based and SMA) received a modern contraceptive method. This is an increase from 77% in FY22.
Ipas conducted global advocacy work in strengthening progressive policy and advocacy and countering the opposition, in partnership with the UN and other SRHR and reproductive justice statekholders. Providing timely opposition information and support to staff and partners is consistenly carried out and Ipas' opposition monitoring team produces and disseminates a monthly "Eye on the Rights" bulletin, in-depths research reports and tailored dissemination exercises. Examples are:
- A report "Anti-Rights Groups Take Aim at Transnational Trade Agreement" details how three NGOs based in the Global North coordinated attacks on the economic agreement between the EU and its country partners in Africa, the Caribbean and Pacific (ACP-EU Partnership Agreement). Based on the report Ipas convened bilateral donors and select civil society partners ahead of a regional parliamentarian meeting for the ACP-EU.
- In March 2023, Ipas published a report on the anti-LGBTI bill in Ghana, Out of Bounds: Foreign and Digital Influence Targeting LGBTI Rights in Ghana. It has received wide support from civil society partners and LGBTI activists in Ghana, as well as extensive media interest from the New York Times, East Africa correspondent. It was also strategically shared with the U.S. State Department ahead of the U.S. Vice Presidents visit with Ghanaian President Nana Akufo-Addo.
Ipas has developed and disseminated tools and research to support advocates of advancing the global safe abortion movement, such as:
- Abortion VCAT Facilitator's Guide for Global Audiences. This facilitators guide includes activities and materials that take workshop participantsincluding health-care providers, policymakers, donor agencies, staff of international development organizations or community-based organizations, religious leaders or a mix of participantsthrough a process of examining their abortion-related values and setting behavioral intentions that are consciously aligned with those values. Often, this process results in participants setting intentions to support increased access for safe abortion care in accordance with their personal values, even for those who would not choose abortion for themselves.
Ipas has also worked in a cross-cutting scope improving abortion access in humanitarian settings, working at the nexus of climate justice and SRHR, working with sexual and gender based violence, comprehensive sexuality education, disability inclusion and LGBT inclusion. Within this scope, Ipas has worked with advocacy and policy efforts, health system programmatic work, community engagement, development and dissemination of toolkits, leading trainings and so on. Two results in the cross-cutting scope are described below.
One example of result in the humanitarian setting:
- Ipas collaborated with UNFPAs Global Humanitarian Program to build institutional capacity and commitment to SRHR, including safe abortion. They developed a UNFPA-specific VCAT Toolkit, including training curricula and monitoring tools, which incorporates key intersectional content areas jointly identified with UNFPA. In April 2023, Ipas master trainers led the first VCAT training-of-trainers for select UNFPA staff, equipping them to roll this content out across the agency.
One example of result in the nexus of climate justice and SRHR:
- In Nepal, Ipas analyzed the complex relationships between climate change, gender dynamics, and sexual and reproductive health and rights. Their findings revealed visible impacts on household well-being and women's SRHR. Notably, climate change contributed to issues such as SGBV, economic insecurity, and compromised autonomy in SRH decision-making. To address these issues effectively, Ipas recommend community sensitization efforts and policy reforms that integrate gender-responsive and climate-sensitive strategies to mitigate the impacts of climate change on SRHR. They have supported the development of Local Adaptation Plans of Action (LAPAs) integrating gender and SRHR considerations, which were endorsed by seven local governments.
